analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md text excerpts (head side, lines 418+ and 612+). They only add or describe release notes; no executable code, configuration, or mode/rename changes are visible. The notes describe App Attest dead-key rotation, APNs retry, diagnostics outside the signed transcript, public model-demand aggregation with k-anonymity suppression (20 requests / 3 accounts), and admin diagnostics. These concern TB-002, TB-009, TB-011 and T-052..T-058. The documented behaviors (rotation never revokes or grants serving, diagnostics untrusted, rate-limited rotation) are consistent with the existing threat model assumptions. A changelog edit is not a security regression by itself. The underlying source changes (App Attest rotation admission and machine-merge serialization, public demand suppression, rotation budget limits, doctor and report log collection) were not supplied, so their implementation is not verified. Later passes with the code should check that rotation cannot be abused to evade revocation or rate limits, and that the public demand aggregates cannot be de-anonymized. No threat-model gaps are introduced by these changelog text changes alone, although new public model-demand statistics might eventually warrant a threat model entry. I do not claim that is a concrete issue here.
